DIGIT 100.name: Introduction to Digital Humanities
DIGIT 100.description: The traditional theories and methods that underwrote the study of literature, history, and philosophy in the 20th century are now being supplemented with new techniques and tools. Surveys an array of tools, techniques, and cultures related to digital humanities (DH).

DIGIT 110.name: Text Encoding Fundamentals
DIGIT 110.description: Teaches students standardized encoding techniques for archival quality data creation, storage, and analysis.

DIGIT 210.name: Large Scale Text Analysis
DIGIT 210.description: Teaches students programmatic and algorithmic techniques and tools for accessing and analyzing unstructured text.

DIGIT 400.name: Digital Project Design
DIGIT 400.description: Introduces students to the tools and resources available to design and implement a digital project.

DIGIT 410.name: Data Visualization
DIGIT 410.description: In-depth understanding of techniques and software for data visualization. Students are introduced to complex data sets and learn how to present findings in interactive and innovative ways.

DIGIT 430.name: Simulations of Human Behavior
DIGIT 430.description: In Modeling and Simulation, students develop an understanding of the systems, processes, tools, and implications of this field. Prerequisite (not enumerable as specific courses): 3 credits of programming, 3 credits of mathematics. Cross-listed with GAME 430.

DIGIT 494.name: Senior Project
DIGIT 494.description: A senior capstone course that allows students to design, complete, and present an independent digitally based project.

DIGIT 495.name: Internship
DIGIT 495.description: A professional internship opportunity with a business, organization, or non-profit agency.
